study type: Pooled analysis of national birth registry data
exposure: Proportion of the population living in poverty
cohort: The study analyzed 3,376,062 births from the Peruvian national birth registry between 2012 and 2020, focusing on mothers giving birth in Peru.
finding: C-section rates in Peru decreased slightly from 39.7% in 2012 to 38.0% in 2020, remaining above international recommendations, with significant disparities observed by natural region, province, and women's socioeconomic status.
mod_finding: C-section rates in Peru remained above international recommendations (decreasing slightly from 39.7% in 2012 to 38.0% in 2020), with significant disparities observed based on natural region, province, and socioeconomic status.
